definitions.definition: intermittent CT guidance used during biopsy

steps: Obtain helical CT to plan trajectory avoiding vessels, fissures, bullae
Advance coaxial introducer needle under CT fluoroscopy
Perform FNA and/or core biopsy (typically 2–5 passes, ≥4 cores for molecular testing)
Seal tract with saline, hydrogel plug, or ABPI
Place biopsy-side down post-procedure to reduce pneumothorax risk
clinical_procedures.notes: ROSE can be performed to ensure adequacy; samples sent for histopathology, microbiology, molecular studies

diagnostic_approaches.advantages: Higher tissue adequacy, better for histology and molecular analysis
Less invasive, cytology sufficient for many lesions
Improves lesion targeting, reduces inconclusive biopsies

clinical_guidelines.recommendation: Perform coagulation profile before TTNB; INR <1.5 and platelet count >50,000/μL recommended; >100,000/μL if aspirin continued.
Relative contraindications: small deep lesions (<1 cm), lesions near vessels or airways, severe emphysema, pulmonary hypertension, oxygen dependence.
Target viable areas with FDG uptake or enhancing tissue; avoid necrotic areas.
Seal tract with saline, hydrogel plug, or autologous blood patch to reduce pneumothorax risk.

complications.notes: Higher with core biopsy, larger needles, fissure crossing, emphysema; mitigated with tract sealing and patient positioning
Serious complication; managed with 100% O₂ and Trendelenburg/left decubitus
Severe pain should prompt evaluation for complications
